description: We are a team of six engineering students from ENSA Béni Mellal representing our club CSIA. Through the “Field Shift: Adapting Farms with NASA Data” challenge, we aim to build a data-driven solution using NASA Earth observation data to support farmers in making better decisions about water use, crop adaptation, and resilience to changing environmental conditions.
summary:
Flaht Bladi is a mobile-first web app that helps farmers in the Tadla region (Beni Amir / Beni Moussa, Morocco) decide what to plant next, when to plant it, and how to rotate crops between seasons.

The farmer enters simple information about their parcel location, soil type, water access, and past crops. The app then compares the farmer's current plan with two alternative rotation options, explained in plain, farmer-friendly language, and shows a planting calendar for each crop. An interactive map of the Tadla perimeter helps farmers find nearby wholesale markets, seed suppliers, and water-related satellite observations. A simple community feed lets farmers share experiences, sell harvests, and find partners in Darija or English.

We used NASA data to make decisions smarter: NASA POWER for local weather and climate, SMAP for soil moisture, GPM for rainfall, and MODIS vegetation data to understand crop and land conditions. This means advice is based on real Earth observations, not guesswork.

It is important because small farmers face changing weather and water scarcity, and NASA data is free for everyone. The app is built to be scalable: starting from Tadla, the same approach can expand to any region in Morocco or beyond without changing the core design.
details:
What it does / how it works Flaht Bladi is a mobile-first web app that helps farmers in the Tadla region (Beni Amir / Beni Moussa, Morocco) decide what to plant next and how to rotate crops. The farmer answers a simple guided form about their parcel zone, irrigation, water system, last crop. The app runs the answers through a rule engine of 8 agronomic rules (e.g., disease carry-over after cereals, nematode buildup in continuous wheat) and shows the farmer's current strategy next to two ranked alternatives, each with a score out of 100 and a plain-language explanation citing the exact rule behind it. A real interactive Leaflet map of the Tadla perimeter shows source-verified places (dams and reference cities), and a simple community area lets farmers share experiences, harvest offers, and partnership requests all in Darija (local moroccan language) or English, with right-to-left support.

How we used NASA data We used NASA POWER for local weather and climate values, SMAP for soil moisture, GPM for rainfall, and MODIS vegetation data to ground the recommendations in real Earth observations instead of guesswork.

Benefits & intended impact Farmers get transparent decision support scores with reasons, honest labels that distinguish measured data from estimates, and no fake promises about yield or profit. The intended impact is smarter crop rotation, healthier soils, and better water use in a region facing water scarcity.

Tools & technologies Next.js (React), TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, Leaflet for the map, Vitest, Playwright and Testing Library for tests, ESLint, deployed on Vercel.

Creativity & factors we considered We designed for farmers with limited digital literacy: bilingual Darija/English interface, no jargon, and features still under development are clearly labeled rather than faked. We considered data transparency, verified coordinates only, mobile-first access, and scalability the same design can extend from Tadla to any region without structural changes.
